LHX.sentence: L3Harris dropped about 9% this week even though the four bigger defense contractors all rallied, and since nothing changed about the business, it just looks unusually cheap compared to its peers right now.

ASML.sentence: ASML is drifting higher and there's nothing dramatic going on — they're still the only company on earth making a certain essential chipmaking machine, and demand is expected to pick up next year.

LIN.sentence: Linde barely budged, but it's unusually beaten-down for such a steady industrial-gas supplier — a quality name that rarely goes on sale is doing exactly that right now.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft jumped 15% in a single day after strong earnings — the AI-cloud story is clearly working, though the stock has now run up fast and may need to catch its breath.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher was basically flat, but biotech funding is thawing again, and since they sell the lab equipment those companies buy, more orders should start flowing their way over the next several months.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge is quiet and behaving exactly like the oil-and-gas toll road it is, though the extra income it pays over safe government bonds has gotten thin lately.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow has fallen a long way from its high — an unusually big drop for a company whose corporate and government customers keep signing multi-year contracts for its workflow and AI tools.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore rose about 5% as copper prices climbed, and investors are giving extra credit to its trading arm — the part of the business that profits when commodity markets get choppy.

IBIT.sentence: Bitcoin is sitting well below its recent highs and near the bottom of its year's range, so it's in a quiet, depressed patch rather than doing anything alarming.

KOF.sentence: The Latin American Coca-Cola bottler ticked up slightly and looks inexpensive for such a steady, dependable business.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras ticked up with oil prices cooperating and pays a hefty dividend, though the worry is that oil is near a high point and earnings could soften if prices roll over.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk, the Danish container-shipping giant that moves goods across the oceans, edged up slightly and is trading for less than its fleet of ships is worth.

MA.sentence: Mastercard edged up as people keep tapping their cards more than ever — the worry that new payment technology could replace card networks is still just a fear, with no real evidence of it happening yet.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot company was flat on the day but is unusually cheap for a business where every operation on its machines sells more supplies, giving it a rare stream of repeat revenue that the market isn't fully paying up for.
